宏福苑獨立委員會聆訊披露，管理公司「置邦興業」曾編製一份「授權黃碧嬌的單位」檔案，顯示 2021 年 12 月 11 日選聘顧問「鴻毅」的業主大會上，有 131 張授權票與黃碧嬌團隊有關，佔當日整體授權票約 25%。《集誌社》取得授權記錄後發現，131 張授權票授權了連同黃碧嬌在內的 53 人，以此 53 人名單統計，當日黃碧嬌「友好」授權票多達 252 張，佔整體近五成。龐大網絡有何背景？其中，有 5 人與太和邨舊法團委員同名同姓，該法團在 2016 年因天價工程爭議被推翻；部分太和舊法團委員在 2021 年 12 月亦「跨邨」現身宏福苑業主大會。翻查資料，當年涉及太和邨維修爭議的顧問「浩熙」以低價中標，該公司曾參與宏福苑工程投標；「浩熙」擔任大圍景田苑顧問時，工程由「宏業」中標，曾被業主入稟質疑圍標。記者透過短訊、電郵、區議員辦事處向黃碧嬌查詢，截稿前未獲回覆。相關報道：追查黃碧嬌授權票．2 ︳53 人取得 131 張授權票　他們是誰？　部分人具民建聯、新社聯等背景 追查黃碧嬌授權票．3 ︳兩名業主離世後　姓名出現「授權黃碧嬌單位」名單　家人不知情

The independent committee hearing of Wang Fuk Court revealed that at the owners' meeting held on 11 December 2021 to appoint consultant "Hung Ngai", 131 proxy votes were related to the Wong Bik-kiu team; the agenda that day included the appointment of "Hung Ngai" as works consultant and a demand to remove the old owners' corporation. (Owners' corporation photo)

The hearing revealed that Wong Bik-kiu initially admitted to having received only about 20 proxy votes, but the committee found a file named "Units authorising Wong Bik-kiu" in the records of management company "Hop On", which documented that she had 131 proxy votes at the 2021 meeting, representing about 25% of all proxy votes that day. Most of the 131 proxy votes did not name Wong Bik-kiu as the proxy holder. She later explained through her lawyer that the figure was a "combined tally" involving volunteer teams, incumbent owners' corporation committee members and community friends, who together "assisted in handling" 131 votes, while only about 20-odd were specifically designated to her personally.

"Collective Journal" obtained multiple proxy vote records from Wang Fuk Court owners' meetings, including proxy lists from the owners' meetings on 25 January 2019 to appoint "Hung Ngai" as registered inspector (RI), 11 December 2021 to appoint "Hung Ngai" as consultant, 28 January 2024 to appoint "Wang Yip" as contractor, 6 September 2024 to appoint a new owners' corporation, as well as the "Units authorising Wong Bik-kiu" file.

In December 2021, former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation chairperson Tam Lai-har (left), treasurer Shek Yuk-chun (front centre), committee member Ng Ling-lan (back centre) and Mok Shuk-ching (right) appeared at the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting. On that day, Mok Shuk-ching was seen standing near the "Proxy Vote Registration Counter" holding a stack of papers. (Photo provided by interviewee)

Former Tai Wo Estate Owners' Corporation Involved in Repair Controversy Appears at Wang Fuk Court Meeting

The 131 proxy votes at the December 2021 owners' meeting involved 129 owners, with 53 first proxy holders including Wong Bik-kiu. Among them, "Tam Lai-har", "Shek Yuk-chun", "Mok Shuk-ching", "Yiu Kam-sheung" and "Ng Ling-lan" each held 3 to 4 proxy votes, totalling 17. These five people share the same names as former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation committee members — Tam Lai-har was former chairperson, Shek Yuk-chun was former treasurer, and the other three were former committee members.

Former Tai Wo Estate mutual aid committee member A (alias), who was concerned about repair and owners' corporation disputes, went to the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting in December 2021 to observe. She recalled that upon arrival, she noticed several former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation committee members present, including Tam Lai-har, Shek Yuk-chun, Mok Shuk-ching and Ng Ling-lan. "I found it very strange at the time, it was as if they were the hosts, the whole venue was like Wong Bik-kiu doing the welcoming... It's not unusual for one or two people to come, but an entire team, boss... My gut feeling was that they were involved again?" A provided photos from that day, pointing out that Mok Shuk-ching was standing beside the "Proxy Vote Registration Counter" holding a stack of papers, constantly making phone calls "wandering back and forth" and "queuing to collect voting forms".

Tai Wo Estate experienced a massive repair bid-rigging controversy in 2016. The then owners' corporation eventually re-tendered, with the project cost reduced from HK$27 million to HK$500,000 to HK$700,000, and the owners' corporation was subsequently overthrown.

Regarding the Tai Wo Estate bid-rigging controversy, A pointed out that residents had asked the Housing Department's ICU, which supervised the works, and learned that the government repair order only involved a small portion of external wall areas of buildings with falling concrete. However, the owners' corporation decided without consulting residents to repair the full external walls of three buildings, and used the rationale that the estate's maintenance fund had over HK$100 million and residents would not need to contribute money to lobby residents. When residents tried to understand the decision, they were refused entry to meetings by the owners' corporation on the grounds that meetings were limited to five people.

Records show that rental-purchased public housing estate Tai Wo Estate became embroiled in an inflated repair controversy in 2016. Tam Lai-har and Shek Yuk-chun were the chairperson and treasurer of the then owners' corporation, while Yiu Kam-sheung, Mok Shuk-ching and Ng Ling-lan were committee members. The owners' corporation at the time engaged consultant "Ho Hei Architecture Engineering Consultants Company" to conduct external wall inspections, with consultancy fees of approximately HK$150,000. The quotation for external wall repairs of three buildings reached as high as HK$27 million, requiring each household to bear over HK$10,000. The project costs sparked bid-rigging controversy. Following residents' efforts, the project was re-tendered and costs were reduced to HK$500,000 to HK$700,000. The old owners' corporation was overthrown that same year.

Tam Lai-har (seventh from left) ran in the 2003 District Council election as a DAB candidate and lost. She served as chairperson of Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation from the early 2000s until being overthrown in 2016. The photo shows a group photo at the 2015 Tai Po Rural Committee inauguration ceremony dinner; Wong Bik-kiu is second from left. (Facebook photo)

Former Tai Wo Estate Owners' Corporation Chairperson Was DAB Associate

Former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation chairperson Tam Lai-har, who obtained proxy votes at Wang Fuk Court and appeared on the "Authorising Wong Bik-kiu" list, has a DAB background. She represented the party in the 2003 Tai Po District Council election and lost, while her party associate Wong Bik-kiu won. In 2006, Tam was appointed as an added member of the Tai Po District Council Culture, Recreation and Sports Committee. During the New Territories East by-election in September 2016, she canvassed for DAB candidates Chan Hak-kan and Chow Ho-ting. Former committee member Mok Shuk-ching served alongside Wong Bik-kiu on the Tai Po District Fight Crime Committee in 2009, and in 2021 became a specially invited director of the New Forum; Yiu Kam-sheung is also a New Forum Tai Po district director; as for Shek Yuk-chun and Ng Ling-lan, they are current members of the Tai Po Po Nga Area Care Team.

Besides the December 2021 owners' meeting to appoint "Hung Ngai", "Shek Yuk-chun" and "Ng Ling-lan" also each received one proxy vote at the September 2024 owners' meeting to appoint a new owners' corporation, when "Wong Chun-yau" was listed as another proxy holder. Records show that "Wong Chun-yau" and Wong Bik-kiu co-founded the "Lok Kwan Volunteer Alliance".

The reporter contacted Wong Bik-kiu via text message, email and the district councillor's office for comment, but received no response before deadline.

Wong Bik-kiu founded the "Lok Kwan Volunteer Alliance" with Wong Chun-yau (left) and Ting Kit-mui (right). On the "Units authorising Wong Bik-kiu" list, there are people with the same names as authorised persons, as well as individuals with names related to "Lok Kwan Volunteers" who were authorised. (Facebook photo)

Tai Wo Estate Consultant Once Bid for Wang Fuk Court; Wang Yip Won Contract for King Tin Court Project

"Ho Hei", which received ultra-low consultancy fees at Tai Wo Estate, was founded by Wong Siu-cheung, who also submitted bids for Wang Fuk Court projects. "Ho Hei" bid HK$700,000 for the Wang Fuk Court registered inspector (RI) in January 2019, higher than "Hung Ngai"'s HK$220,000, and failed to win the contract.

By 2021, "Tai Tei Architecture Consultants Limited", in which Wong Siu-cheung was a director, bid HK$400,000 for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy, slightly higher than "Hung Ngai"'s HK$300,000, and failed to win. "Fai Lei Tat Architecture Engineering Consultants Limited" bid HK$280,000 for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy and similarly failed; Wong Siu-cheung became a director of "Fai Lei Tat" the following year.

According to court documents, in 2009, Sha Tin King Tin Court appointed "Ho Hei" as works consultant. Following a 2011 tender, "Wang Yip" was appointed as contractor for a project worth HK$91 million. An owner filed a lawsuit in 2012 alleging the project involved bid-rigging and sought to overturn the decision, but lost.

The company that won the Tai Wo Estate repair consultancy at a low price in 2016 subsequently bid for the Wang Fuk Court registered inspector; a related company also bid for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy. Both bid prices were higher than Hung Ngai's and neither succeeded.

Wong Siu-cheung and Wong Siu-keung, who was previously involved in the Sha Tin Villa Esplanade bid-rigging case, are suspected to be related parties. During the trial of the Sha Tin Villa Esplanade HK$260 million bid-rigging case, it was revealed that "Universal Housing" director Wong Siu-keung paid "tea money" and referral fees to owners' corporation members and works subcontractors, and arranged for shell companies to submit bids, enabling "Universal Housing" to win the contract. In 2023, Wong Siu-keung was arrested in connection with a HK$160 million bid-rigging case involving Discovery Bay. Company searches show that a construction company in which Wong Siu-cheung was previously a director, now dissolved, once shared the same registered address with one used by Wong Siu-keung.
